summary.text: Torque is the rotational counterpart of force: a twist applied to an object about a chosen axis, also called the moment of force.
Its size is the part of the force acting perpendicular to the lever arm, multiplied by that arm's length.
Its SI unit is the newton-metre, which matches the joule dimensionally even though torque and energy are different physical quantities.

facts.label: Other names
facts.value: Moment of force, or simply moment

items.prompt: You push a heavy door with the same force near the hinges, then at the handle. Why does the handle feel easier?

options.label: The hinges absorb part of the force
The twist grows with distance from the pivot
Doors only swing when pushed at the handle
Your force itself grows at the handle

items.explain: Torque is the perpendicular force times the distance from the pivot, so a longer arm gives more twist for the same push.

items.prompt: You push on a wrench handle straight toward the bolt, along the handle's length. How much twist do you produce?

options.label: The maximum, since you aim at the bolt
Half the maximum
It depends on the bolt size
None, since only the perpendicular part counts

items.explain: Torque uses the perpendicular component of the force, which is zero for a push along the arm.

items.prompt: Newton-metres and joules have the same base dimensions. Does that make torque a kind of energy?

options.label: No, torque is a vector and energy a scalar
Yes, they are the same thing
Yes, but only for turning shafts
No, since their dimensions differ

items.explain: The dimensional match does not mean the physical quantities are the same; torque is a vector and energy is a scalar.

items.prompt: A US mechanical engineer says moment and a US physicist says torque. Are they describing different things?

options.label: Yes, moment is for straight pushes
Yes, torque is only for engines
No, one quantity with field-dependent names
No, but a moment is always smaller

items.explain: Torque is also called the moment of force, with the word choice depending on field and place.

items.prompt: A 20 N force acts perpendicular to a wrench, 0.5 m from the bolt. What is the torque?

options.label: 40 N⋅m
10 N⋅m

items.explain: Multiply the perpendicular force by the lever arm: 20 times 0.5 gives 10 N⋅m.

items.prompt: A force tends to produce motion along a line. What does a torque tend to produce?

options.label: Twisting around an axis
Heat around a point
Sliding along a surface
Stretching along a rod

items.explain: Torque is defined as that which produces or tends to produce torsion around an axis.
